card.summary: Animate the current image into a short clip: SparseCtrl pins the first frame to your image, IP-Adapter keeps the subject, and the motion module animates it. Subpar SD1.5 quality but the subject is preserved and moves.

prompt.guidance: Describe the SCENE/subject in your image. AnimateDiff adds generic motion on its own; the prompt does NOT direct the motion (use Wan/LTX for prompt-directed motion).
prompt.overview: The text prompt sets the SCENE, subject, and STYLE (an ordinary SD-style prompt); motion is generic/automatic from the motion module, not precisely prompt-directed.
prompt.instructions: Write a normal SD-style prompt (booru tags for anime checkpoints, a short natural-language phrase for photoreal) describing subject, setting, lighting, and art style to match your checkpoint. For i2v the actual motion comes from the SparseCtrl-RGB start frame plus the motion module, NOT the words - the prompt barely steers HOW things move, so you mostly get generic ambient motion. To direct motion, add a motion-LoRA (zoom in/out, pan left/right, tilt, rolling) rather than prose. The distilled variants (AnimateLCM, AnimateDiff-Lightning) use the same prompt style but run few steps at low/no CFG, so keep prompts and negatives shorter and avoid high CFG. Be realistic: this gives SD-style scene/style control but only weak, generic motion control compared to Wan/LTX.
do: Prompt like a still SD image: subject + setting + lighting + style, in your checkpoint's tag/phrase convention
Match the prompt and checkpoint to the start frame so conditioning and text agree
Add quality/style anchor tags ('masterpiece, best quality, detailed') to reduce flicker
Use a motion-LoRA token for camera movement (zoom, pan, tilt, rolling) when you need directed motion
Add a light action hint ('hair blowing in wind', 'walking forward') as a nudge, not a command
For AnimateLCM / Lightning keep prompts concise and run low steps at low/no CFG
Use SD-style negative prompts - they materially improve quality here
dont: Don't write cinematic frame-by-frame motion choreography expecting it to execute - AnimateDiff won't follow it
Don't request complex/unusual motion outside the module's training (it produces generic movement)
Don't crank CFG or pile on emphasis weights with the distilled (LCM/Lightning) variants
Don't expect the prompt to override the start frame's motion in i2v
Don't omit the negative prompt; an empty negative noticeably degrades output
examples: 1girl, long silver hair, school uniform, standing on rooftop, sunset, cinematic lighting, wind, hair blowing in the wind, masterpiece, best quality, highly detailed
a lone astronaut walking across a red desert under a pink sky, dust drifting, soft volcanic light, photorealistic
prompt.negative_guidance: Use standard SD-style negatives (e.g. 'worst quality, low quality, blurry, deformed, bad anatomy, watermark, text') - they apply and meaningfully improve coherence; keep them lighter for the AnimateLCM/Lightning low-CFG variants.

ui_help.note: Animate the current picture into a short clip. The subject is kept; motion is automatic.
ui_help.good_for: turning a still image into a short anime clip

edit_use_cases: image-to-video: animate the current picture, keeping its subject (SD1.5 AnimateDiff + IP-Adapter)
